proposition: Whether the Tamhid was of secondary importance in the estimation of Ibn Turka and his contemporaries is asserted by Melvin-Koushki and contradicted by the modern Iranian tradition that treats it as his definitive work; the pages read support MK's side with the Mafahis introduction, the author's own hierarchies and the Khwandamir and Afandi notices, but none states the ranking outright.

mediation.note: Central to MK's case; the rival (Tamhid-centred) position rests on the Tamhid's later curricular success.
